newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Arafat vows not to give up Palestinian rights.
newsitem.headline: Arafat vows not to give up Palestinian rights.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat declared on Friday he would not compromise on any Palestinian rights following the recent violence in the West Bank and Gaza and his summit talks in Washington.

"The Palestinian position is clear toward the current events and evolutions. It is not possible, in any circumstance, to give up on any of the legitimate Palestinian rights," Arafat told reporters after meeting Tunisian President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali.
Arafat said he had briefed Ben Ali on the Washington summit he attended with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Jordan's King Hussein and U.S. President Bill Clinton.
Arafat, who visited Morocco on Thursday, later left Tunis for Naples to meet Italian government leaders and was expected to fly on to Paris to meet French President Jacques Chirac.

The two-day Washington summit ended on Wednesday with no agreement on major substantive issues that led to fierce Israeli-Palestinian violence last week and threatened to undermine further the already battered peace process.

The only concrete achievement of the summit -- which Palestinian officials declared was a failure -- was an agreement for the two sides to resume open-ended negotiations on Sunday at the border crossing of Erez between Israel and the Palestinian self-rule area of Gaza.
Arafat praised Clinton for what he called his "courageous decision" to host the Washington meeting "despite the difficult circumstances".
The PLO said on Friday it would welcome U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher's attendance at Sunday's talks.

Diplomatic sources in Washington on Thursday said U.S. Mideast Coordinator Dennis Ross was discussing the arrangements with Israeli and Palestinian leaders. Some sources said the trip was extremely likely, but a final decision had not been made.
"We welcome any U.S. official who comes. We are ready if he (Christopher) decides to come," Arafat's spokesman Nabil abu Rdainah said.
Abu Rdainah said the PLO had no intention of renegotiating its agreement with Israel on the redeployment of Israeli troops from Hebron, an issue that is expected to top the agenda on Sunday.
"There will not be any renegotiation of the agreement on Hebron. This is a meeting to implement (agreements) and agree a timetable for that," he said.
He confirmed that the Palestinian delegation to the talks would be headed by chief negotiator Saeb Erekat and that Arafat would not attend.
Israel wants to renegotiate the security arrangements it says are necessary to protect about 400 Jewish settlers living in the heart of the city of 120,000 Palestinians.
Palestinians insist Netanyahu to implement an agreement on redeploying Israeli troops that was signed with Israel's previous government defeated by Netanyahu in May elections.
